## Not yet defensible

- Out-of-fold predictions on the development rows are used to compare the models and the variant, so they are development evidence, not independent evidence of future performance. Only the sealed final test, opened once, is.
- The data were explored or published before this study; its rows are not unseen.
- Rows that share a value of car_name can fall in several folds: this version does not group the folds by it, so the split reports how many group values the folds share instead of preventing it. A row predicted out of fold is then not independent of the rows of its group the model was fitted on.
- Some results are stale and must be recomputed before they are cited.
- Associations in observational data do not show that acting on a variable would change the outcome.
- Experiments in the notebook workbench are not recorded and are not decisions.
